newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel intent on making Bezeq offer soon.
newsitem.headline: Israel intent on making Bezeq offer soon.

text.p: Israel is intent on moving swiftly to further privatise Bezeq Israel Telecom, even though Bezeq itself would prefer to concentrate on floating shares overseas, officials said on Wednesday.

Officials at Bezeq, which is 76 percent-owned by the government and is Israel's main telecommunications carrier, said they fear that once a planned domestic issue is completed, long-running plans for a global offering could fall by the wayside.
The company, said one official said, sees a global offering as crucial for its future.

Bezeq will have huge financing needs in the next few years and needs to diversify sources and become better recognised in international financial markets. A global offering would provide a "sophisticated base of international investors," he explained.

Communications Minister Limor Livnat agreed on February to a proposal for a domestic offering, saying the government wanted to show quick progress on privatisation. Until now, the government had been planning to float shares overseas.

"We intend to do an international offering but the window is more towards the end of year," said Tsipi Livni, who heads the Government Corporations Authority, adding: "There's been no decision to cancel the international tender."
She said it was too early to say when the offering would take place.
Livni said the government's decision to proceed with a domestic offering was to encourage the local capital market and because it could be done more quickly.

But one source close to the Bezeq offering said the key reason was that government officials believed they could float the company domestically without reaching an agreement with its second-biggest shareholder, Britain's Cable and Wireless PLC.
Cable snapped up 10 percent of Bezeq in the stock market two years ago and has since sought to increase its stake and become a strategic partner.
The source said investors would look askance at any Bezeq offering for fear Cable might sell its shares at some point.

The Cable holding, which makes up almost half of Bezeq's float, has inflated the share price by keeping supply tight, the source said. If Cable sold, he estimated the price could fall to six or seven shekels ($1.80-$2.10) a share from its current 8.5 shekels.
The source said officials believe investors in Israel would be less concerned than those overseas about Cable dumping shares, adding that he disagreed.

But Debra Kodish, director of research at Zannex Securities, said she believed officials were probably right. Relations between Cable and Bezeq were good, and the British company had no intentions of bailing out for now.
The government has been in long-running talks to reach a stand-still agreement with Cable, which Livni said is aimed at preventing Cable's dumping the shares.
Irrespective of the Cable issue, Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex, said that with the Tel Aviv stock market's recent revival after a three-year slump, local investors could absorb an issue.
"The market is ripe for IPOs from the government," he said.
A source close to the Bezeq offering said a domestic and global offering, done in parallel or timed closely together, could succeed. But the domestic offering would have to be small.
"If they do it in small tranches, of 300 million or 500 million shekels, they could get it done," he said.
The Government Corporations Authority has authorisation dating back to 1993 to float up to 1.4 billion shekels. Bezeq current market capitalisation is about 6.2 billion shekels.
